message.content: The structured data lacks recent railway operating expense facts, so I'll rely on the report's disclosed ratio and verify the arithmetic from the disclosed revenue/expense figures.

**Norfolk Southern's railway operating ratio improved sharply in 2024 (fiscal year ended December 31, 2024).**

**Headline result**
- The railway operating ratio — railway operating expenses ÷ railway operating revenues, i.e., the share of revenue consumed by expenses — fell to **66.4% in 2024 from 76.5% in 2023**, an improvement of **10.1 percentage points** (lower is better). The company itself describes this as "improved to 66.4 percent" (2024 Form 10-K, MD&A, chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:86400).
- On the company's **adjusted (non-GAAP)** basis, the ratio improved more modestly, from **67.4% in 2023 to 65.8% in 2024**, a **1.6 percentage-point** improvement (non-GAAP reconciliation, chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:91200).

**Underlying figures (2024 vs. 2023, $ millions)**
- Railway operating revenues: $12,123 vs. $12,156 (roughly flat, −0.3%)
- Railway operating expenses: $8,052 vs. $9,305 (−13%)
- Income from railway operations: $4,071 vs. $2,851 (+43%)

I verified the reported ratios arithmetically from these disclosed figures: 8,052/12,123 = 66.4% and 9,305/12,156 = 76.5% (tool-calculated). Revenue for 2024 is also in the structured data as $12.123 billion (fact id 859736, accession 0000702165-25-000008, FY 2024, end_date 2024-12-31); the 2023 comparative is $12.156 billion (fact id 859727, same accession).

**Why it moved**
The 2024 improvement was driven mainly by **lower operating expenses**, not higher revenue. Per the 10-K, the expense reduction included lower net costs related to the Eastern Ohio Incident and **$433 million of gains on sales of railway lines** (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:86400). The 2023 ratio of 76.5% was itself inflated by about **$1.1 billion of net Eastern Ohio Incident expenses**; excluding those, the 2023 adjusted ratio was 67.4% (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:91200). So the headline 10.1-point swing largely reflects the absence of 2023's incident costs plus 2024 line-sale gains, while the adjusted comparison (65.8% vs. 67.4%) shows a smaller underlying efficiency gain from lower fuel prices, purchased services and other expenses.

**Context / caveats**
- The five-year statistics table shows the ratio at 62.3% in 2022, 60.1% in 2021 and 69.3% in 2020 (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:9600), so 2024's 66.4% is better than 2023 but still worse than 2021–2022.
- The structured financial-facts table did not contain recent railway operating expense tags (its OperatingExpenses series ends in 2019), so the expense figures above come from the 2024 annual report text rather than the SQL facts table. The ratios are as disclosed by the company and independently reproduced from the disclosed revenue and expense amounts.
